aws.overview: Monkey continuously assesses the security configuration of your AWS account through a read-only role. It discovers its servers, databases, storage and functions, lets you choose which ones belong to each service and turns every result into input for your controls' automated tests.
features: Discover the account's resources in the regions you declare
Choose which resources belong to each service
Assess identity and privileged access, encryption and network exposure, logging, alerts and backups
Repeat the assessment every 6 or 24 hours
See each finding with its control code, its impact and how to fix it
prerequisites: Permission in your AWS account to create an IAM role or deploy a CloudFormation template
Your AWS account number and the regions where the service runs

security_audit.name: SecurityAudit
security_audit.detail: Read the security configuration of the account's services.

view_only_access.name: ViewOnlyAccess
view_only_access.detail: List and view resources without reading the content of your data.

assume_role.name: Assume the role
assume_role.detail: Only Monkey, with your company's external ID, and for sessions of one hour at most.

security.read_only: The role cannot create, change or delete anything in your account.
security.temporary_credentials: Each assessment uses one-hour temporary credentials; with the recommended role Monkey does not store keys to your account.
security.external_id: Only Monkey, with the identifier it generates for your company, can assume the role.
security.isolated_execution: Each assessment runs in an isolated environment that is deleted when it finishes.
security.tenant_isolation: Your account's results are visible only to your company.
security.encrypted_keys: If you choose the access keys channel, they are stored encrypted and never shown.
